name: Swift API Design Guidelines
description: Rules based on Swift.org API Design Guidelines (https://www.swift.org/documentation/api-design-guidelines)

rules.name: Clarity at Point of Use
rules.description: Include all needed words, omit needless words
rules.message: Consider removing redundant words like 'get', 'make', 'do' from method names. Swift prefers concise names at call site.

rules.name: Boolean Properties Read as Assertions
rules.description: Boolean properties and methods should read as assertions about the receiver
rules.message: Boolean properties should read as assertions (e.g., 'isEmpty', 'hasPrefix') rather than stating they are booleans

rules.name: Protocols Describing What Something Is
rules.description: Protocols that describe what something is should read as nouns
rules.message: Protocols describing capabilities should use 'able', 'ible' suffix (e.g., Equatable, ProgressReporting)

rules.name: Mutating vs Non-mutating Methods
rules.description: Mutating methods should use verb form, non-mutating should use past participle or gerund
rules.message: Mutating methods should use imperative verb (e.g., 'sort'), non-mutating use past participle (e.g., 'sorted')

rules.name: Factory Method Naming
rules.description: Factory methods should begin with 'make'
rules.message: Factory methods returning Self should typically begin with 'make' (e.g., 'makeIterator')

rules.name: Parameter Names for Type Conversions
rules.description: When initializer performs value preserving type conversion, omit first argument label
rules.message: For value-preserving type conversions, omit first argument label (e.g., 'init(_ value: Int)' not 'init(from value: Int)')

rules.name: Compensate for Weak Type Information
rules.description: Compensate for weak type information in parameter names
rules.message: When parameter type is weakly constrained (Any, AnyObject), include role-describing noun in parameter name

rules.name: Argument Labels for Prepositional Phrases
rules.description: When first argument forms part of prepositional phrase, give it an argument label
rules.message: When method name includes preposition, first argument should have a label (e.g., 'removeBoxes(havingLength:)')

rules.name: Avoid Abbreviations
rules.description: Avoid obscure abbreviations
rules.message: Avoid abbreviations. Use full words for clarity (e.g., 'button' not 'btn', 'manager' not 'mgr')

rules.name: Embrace Precedent
rules.description: Don't optimize terms of art
rules.message: Use established terms from domain (List, Array, etc.) rather than inventing new terminology

rules.name: Prefer Method and Property Names
rules.description: Prefer methods and properties to free functions
rules.message: Consider whether this free function would be better as a method or property

rules.name: Follow Case Conventions
rules.description: Types and protocols are UpperCamelCase, everything else is lowerCamelCase
rules.message: Functions, variables, and constants should use lowerCamelCase, not UpperCamelCase

rules.name: Type Names as UpperCamelCase
rules.description: Types should use UpperCamelCase
rules.message: Type names (class, struct, enum, protocol) must use UpperCamelCase

rules.name: Enum Cases as lowerCamelCase
rules.description: Enumeration cases should use lowerCamelCase
rules.message: Enumeration cases should use lowerCamelCase (e.g., 'case someValue' not 'case SomeValue')

rules.name: Prefer Terminology Well
rules.description: Use terminology consistent with existing culture
rules.message: Use standard collection terminology: append/insert/remove for elements, not 'Item'

rules.name: Document Complexity
rules.description: Document computational complexity if not O(1)
rules.message: Document computational complexity for operations that are not O(1)

rules.name: Closure Parameters Should Be Unnamed
rules.description: Closure parameters at call site should typically be unnamed
rules.message: Closure parameters are typically unnamed at call site (e.g., '{ x in }' not '{ (x: Int) in }')

rules.name: Use Default Parameters
rules.description: Take advantage of defaulted parameters when simplifying common uses
rules.message: Consider using default parameters instead of overloading methods

rules.name: Prefer Labeled Arguments
rules.description: Label closure and tuple parameters
rules.message: Consider labeling tuple parameters for clarity at use site

rules.name: Choose Good Parameter Names
rules.description: Provide useful argument labels
rules.message: Avoid excessive use of unlabeled parameters. Labels improve clarity at call sites.

rules.name: Avoid Returning Optional Collection
rules.description: Prefer empty collection over nil
rules.message: Prefer returning empty collection instead of optional collection. Return [] instead of nil.

rules.name: Side Effect Naming
rules.description: Methods with side effects should use imperative verb phrases
rules.message: Methods with side effects should use imperative verbs. Boolean queries should be non-mutating.
